title: Trump says immigration crackdown was 'too tough' and played part in midterms defeat
summary:
US President Donald Trump has said his immigration crackdown was "too tough", marking one of his clearest public retreats from a defining plank of his political agenda, following his party's drubbing in the midterm elections.
In an interview with CBS' 60 Minutes programme, Trump said he believed he deserved an "A plus" for drastically limiting illegal border crossings, but he had been politically "hurt" by sweeping deportations.
The president told 60 Minutes that immigration "both helped and hurt" his fellow Republicans in Tuesday's midterms.
Trump also said he'd "love to do something on immigration" with congressional Democrats, without offering details.
In a previous interview with 60 Minutes a year ago, a defiant Trump insisted his administraiton's immigration raids "haven't gone far enough".

summary:

title: Supreme Court lifts pause on border construction in Big Bend, Texas
summary:
The Supreme Court is paving the way for the Trump administration to resume border construction throughout the Big Bend region in Texas, including inside Big Bend National Park.
The Supreme Court ruled 8-1 Monday that the government “is exceedingly likely to prevail” in its argument that a district court lacked jurisdiction to pause construction when it issued a preliminary injunction in October.
The Trump administration’s plans to build a combination of physical walls, access roads and vehicle barriers in the Big Bend region have sparked bipartisan backlash.
The plans for Big Bend National Park initially included a physical wall, but after public outcry, the plans were changed to include only a combination of vehicle barriers, roads and surveillance technology.
Plaintiffs challenging the construction in court argued in part that DHS exceeded its authority when it waived several environmental and conservation laws to expedite the construction.

title: US Supreme Court allows border wall in Big Bend National Park to proceed
summary:
A lawsuit had sought to block border wall construction in the Big Bend National Park by targeting the waivers that sidestep environmental protections.
Share US Supreme Court allows border wall in Big Bend National Park to proceed on social mediaThe United States Supreme Court has allowed President Donald Trump’s administration to build a border wall through a remote section of Big Bend National Park in West Texas.
The border wall has long been a signature part of Trump’s platform to restrict immigration into the US.
Big Bend National Park includes mountain ranges and desert that serve as a home to endangered species like the Mexican long-nosed bat.
The lawsuit challenged waivers used by the agency to fast-track border construction and sidestep environmental and conservation laws.

title: At least 21 migrants and refugees die trying to reach Greece’s Crete
summary:
Greece’s coastguard said more than 100 people rescued in several operations off the southern coast of Crete.
Share At least 21 migrants and refugees die trying to reach Greece’s Crete on social mediaAt least 21 people have died while trying to reach the Greek island of Crete, a key hub for refugees and migrants trying to reach Europe, authorities said.
The Greek coastguard said it recovered 12 bodies and rescued 18 people from one boat that was spotted by a Morocco-flagged container ship south of the island early on Monday.
In a separate incident, the Greek coastguard recovered eight bodies and rescued 28 refugees and migrants from a boat off southern Crete on Saturday evening.
Two other boats, one carrying about 47 people and another with about 40 people on board, were also found sailing south of Crete.

title: Trump says his immigration policy ‘too tough’ for voters
summary:
Trump concedes some voters were unhappy with his administration’s controversial deportation drive.
Share Trump says his immigration policy ‘too tough’ for voters on social mediaUnited States President Donald Trump has said his immigration policy may have been too extreme for voters, conceding that his deportation policy had damaged his Republican Party’s performance in the last week’s midterm elections.
He said he may be able to work with the new Democratic-controlled Congress on some kind of immigration agreement.
Democrats have said oversight of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Department of Homeland Security is a priority for the new Congress.
During his interview, Trump said a moderate immigration deal would still deport criminals, but allow “good people” who had lived and worked in the country “paying taxes” to stay.
